text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Russian newspapers this morning. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
KOMMERSANT DAILY
- The biggest Russian telecoms holding company, Svyazinvest, which will auction a 25 percent plus one share stake, is encouraging potential buyers.
- The State Duma has widened its control over privatisation by passing a law under which the government will have to seek deputies' approval of privatisation targets.

- Officials of Almazy Rossii Sakha, Russia's dominant diamond producer, are accusing Finance Ministry and the State precious metals reserves of trying to establish control over Russian diamond exports.
- A new top manager has been appointed to the West Siberian Metallurgical combine (Zabsib) to prevent its bankruptcy.
- Vneshkombank, the main state debt dealer, has started to revamp its administration by changing up to half of its staff.
- One of Russia's biggest international airports, St Petersburg's Pulkovo, is planning to raise credits worth $280 million.
- The Duma has passed a law on the rights of foreigners in Russia.
- The art director of the Bolshoi Theatre, Vladimir Vasilyev, said the theatre may not open for a 1997-1998 season because of financial difficuties.
SEVODNYA
- Lev Rokhlin, a leading parliament military expert, has accused President Boris Yeltsin of ruining Russia's armed forces and said the country risked losing its territory east of the Urals.
- Dmitry Tulin, the new chairman of Vneshtorgbank, spells out his views on reforms at the bank, one of the biggest state controlled banks in Russia.
- The Duma failed to approve before its holidays the government's programme of social reforms.
NEZAVISIMAYA GAZETA
- Russia gained the maximum it could from the Denver summit, according to the deputy head of the president's administration, Alexander Livshits.
- Some Moscow business circles are trying to get access to the Russia's diamond market, says the paper in connection with a row between Almazy Rossii Sakha and the State Customs Committee.
- Russia is facing a potential problem with post-traumatic stress syndrome now the war in Chechnya is over and young men have returned to a peacetime existence.
- The government has asked the president to sack the justice minister in connection with a video film scandal.
ROSSIISKIYE VESTI
- The paper blames the Communists, who dominate the State Duma, for failing to pass half of the laws the country needs.
PRAVDA-5
- The paper publishes an interview with Russia's Security Council Secretary, Ivan Rybkin.
MOSKOVSKY KOMSOMOLETS
- Moscow's biggest car plant AZLK has initiated a scheme to sell its Moskvich vehicles by installments, the first time such a loan plan has been introduced by a Russian automobile firm.
- A group of ultra-left political parties have started a campaign of support for North Korea under a general slogan: "A kilo of rice for my Korean friend".
--Tatyana Ustinova, Moscow newsroom, +7095 941 8520.
